items.title: 刚花600亿买下Cursor，马斯克又要对Devin下手
items.summary_en: SpaceX approached Cognition, the developer of AI software engineer Devin, about a potential acquisition, but CEO Scott Wu publicly rejected the offer. Cognition is valued at up to $26 billion with ARR approaching $1 billion and growing 50% month-over-month. Despite rejecting the buyout, Cognition remains in talks to rent compute power from SpaceX's Colossus cluster of over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs.

items.title: Runlayer, Rippling drop lawsuits — but the brouhaha is still a cautionary tale for founders
items.summary_en: Runlayer and Rippling dropped their mutual lawsuits with no settlement, no financial damages, and no lawyers' fees paid. Rippling, having tested Runlayer's MCP gateway for over a year without becoming a customer, immediately released its own competing MCP gateway product after the case ended. Runlayer, which raised $42 million and is led by third-time founder Andrew Berman, had alleged contractual violations, while Rippling countersued on patent claims—a move many saw as an effort to pressure Runlayer into dropping its suit amid mounting legal costs.

items.title: A shot-scraper-style JSON API on Bun 1.4's new Bun.WebView
items.why_now_en: Bun 1.4 just launched with built-in Chromium automation—no playwright needed.
items.summary_en: Bun 1.4, the first stable release after its Rust rewrite, brings significant performance gains including a 5x reduction in idle CPU usage, up to 35% less memory consumption, and over 2,900 bug fixes, alongside new features like Bun.WebView for browser automation via WebKit or Chromium through CDP. The article demonstrates a shot-scraper-style JSON API built with Bun.WebView that loads web pages and executes JavaScript, requiring a 192MB–256MB container when running a full Chrome instance against complex pages.

items.title: Claude adds protein design to its resume
items.summary_en: Anthropic's Claude models (Mythos Preview and Opus 4.8) autonomously ran protein-design campaigns using only one expert-written prompt, internet access, and tools, achieving 22–35% success rates on 14 out of 15 targets—well above the typical 10–15% industry norm—with lab validation by Twist Bioscience and Adaptyv Bio. Opus 5 additionally demonstrated rapid accuracy by measuring a sample at 96.4% purity in 19 minutes versus four days for the lab's own report.

items.title: 消息称 OpenAI 首席财务官告知员工：公司最迟将于 2027 年上市
items.summary_en: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar announced the company aims to go public by 2027, possibly sooner, following a $122 billion funding round in March and an $852 billion valuation. OpenAI's Q2 revenue reached $6.7 billion, with annualized revenue exceeding $40 billion and its AI productivity tools surpassing 20 million weekly active users. Rival Anthropic has also secretly filed for an IPO and reported $65 billion in annualized revenue as of late July, potentially listing as early as September.

items.title: Staggering 90% of biomedical papers now show signs of AI help
items.summary_en: A Nature analysis found that approximately 90% of biomedical papers published in December now show signs of AI assistance, a figure far exceeding prior estimates of Large Language Model use. The data, drawn from PubMed archives, was published online on 20 August 2026.

items.title: Your agent asked for approval. Where did the answer go?
items.summary_en: Current agent interoperability protocols like MCP and A2A coordinate tasks but lack governance capabilities, leaving AI decision-making untraceable and unverifiable. A paper by Kang and Diponegoro scores five protocols against six governance dimensions and concludes that governance remains a missing architectural layer. Effective audit trails require cryptographically signed, content-hashed decision records—anchored in external transparency logs like the IETF's SCITT—that capture not just approvals but also human edits, rationale, and whether interventions refined or replaced the agent's original output.

items.title: Google gives publishers a new way to fight AI-driven traffic losses
items.summary_en: Google is letting publishers embed a "Preferred Sources" button on their sites, allowing readers to mark trusted outlets for preferential treatment across Google Search, Discover, and Google News — a move to counter AI-driven traffic declines that have hurt content-dependent businesses. Since the feature's May launch, over 345,000 unique sources have been selected, and Google says preferred publishers are twice as likely to receive clicks. Additional personalization tools include customizable Discover feeds using natural language commands and tailored audio daily briefings for Android users.

items.title: I’ve spent the last 4 months building a tool that turns resumes into portfolio websites
items.summary_en: itsfolio.tech is a resume-to-portfolio website tool built over 4 months that lets users upload a resume and select a theme to generate a ready-made site. The platform has surpassed 1,000 users and the creator is actively seeking UX feedback to drive further improvements.
